The bug is in [store.py](file:///work/clinicbench/store.py#L165-L171) inside `ToolAPI._cancel`.

When an appointment is cancelled, line 170 updates the freed slot's status to `"booked"` instead of `"open"`:
```python
self.store.slots[a["slot"]].update(status="booked", held_by=None)
```
As a result, `ToolAPI._list` (which filters for `status == "open"`) never lists the slot again, and `ToolAPI._slot_free_for` / `ToolAPI._book` (as well as `ToolAPI._move`) continue to treat it as taken and refuse with `slot_taken`.

Because [store.py](file:///work/clinicbench/store.py) is frozen instrument code listed in [phase3-freeze.json](file:///work/docs/phase3-freeze.json#L9) rather than the driver, this is a `fix`.

```json
{"kind": "fix", "files": ["clinicbench/store.py"], "symbols": ["clinicbench.store.ToolAPI._cancel"], "cause": "ToolAPI._cancel sets the cancelled appointment's slot status to \"booked\" instead of \"open\". Because it stays \"booked\", list_slots omits it and subsequent book or move calls reject it with slot_taken.", "attribution": null}
```

Fixed `ToolAPI._cancel` in [clinicbench/store.py](file:///work/clinicbench/store.py#L165-L171) so cancelling an appointment sets the slot's status to `"open"` instead of `"booked"`.

### Verification
- Ran an inline `python3` check against `ToolAPI` verifying that cancelling an existing appointment sets the slot status to `"open"`, includes the slot in `list_slots()`, and allows rebooking it with `book()` (`OK`). (Note: `pytest` is not installed in the environment, so the `tests/` suite could not be executed.)
